$comment: CANON-25 inversion-proof deferral ledger (#2301). Output of the one-off audit that asked, of
every ABSENCE-asserting gate wired in scripts/check-all.mjs (check-no-*, ratchets, parity):
'which concrete change makes this red?' A gate with an answer carries a flip proof in
scripts/lib/guard-flip-registry.mjs. A gate whose answer could not be reduced to a planted
bad/clean fixture in this pass is a ROW HERE — never an omission.
BANKED, not merely capped: scripts/check-guard-flip.mjs fails when deferred.length != ceiling,
in BOTH directions, AND when `ceiling` differs from the MAX_DEFERRED pin in
scripts/lib/gate-roster.mjs. The pin is deliberately NOT in this file (#2301 review): while
the only comparison was length-vs-ceiling, appending a row and raising the ceiling in one edit
to this file passed the audit outright, which is the opposite of what CANON-25 claimed.
Growing the ledger now means moving MAX_DEFERRED in source; shrinking it means lowering both
in the same commit, so a proven row cannot leave slack for a later silent re-fill.
Every field is machine-verified offline by auditInversionRegistry (scripts/lib/gate-roster.mjs):
`gate` must be in the family derived live from check-all.mjs (a stale or fabricated row fails),
`script`/`category` must agree with that derivation, `reason` must be substantive, and `expires`
must not have passed. `issue` is recorded PROVENANCE and buys nothing on its own: the exemption
is bounded by `expires`, which a clock verifies in every environment. A GitHub-API liveness
check was rejected deliberately — it cannot run offline or in a tokenless job, and a check that
silently no-ops in some environments is the corollary #2301 itself names.

deferred.reason: Counts src/ buckets from process.cwd() against .bloat-baseline.json, and BOOTSTRAPS a missing baseline with exit 0 — so a naive clean fixture passes vacuously. A sound proof must first materialise every BLOAT_BUCKETS path, then invert one.

Compares coverage/coverage-summary.json against .coverage-baseline.json, both at fixed repo-relative paths with no override flag, and bootstraps a missing baseline at exit 0. Inverting it means fabricating a v8 summary artifact.

--gate aggregates jscpd/knip/eslint metrics measured over the live repo from process.cwd() with no root flag; an inversion fixture needs a whole synthetic project plus those external tools, not a planted file.

Scores the live repo from process.cwd() across many registries and compares the result against a committed report; inverting the no-regress arm means fabricating a complete audit report, not a single planted file.

Named in #2301 as structurally dead: it iterates manifest.withheldSafety, absent on all three measured pins, so it prints OK and exits 0 by construction. --manifest makes it fixture-injectable, but the fix and its proof belong to #2291, not to the mechanism issue. Expiry deliberately the shortest in this ledger (#2301 review): every other row means 'not yet proven', this one means 'PROVEN vacuous, fix owned elsewhere' — granting the one gate the audit confirmed checks nothing the same 18-month exemption as the unknowns inverts what CANON-25 is for.

--check walks .github/workflows plus every src/templates/**/*.ejs from process.cwd() with no root flag; a fixture needs both trees, and the by-name last-occurrence indexing defect it hides is #2298's subject, not this issue's.
Reconciles three surfaces (scripts/ci-tools.json, check-all.mjs, the CI workflow + installer) read from fixed repo-relative paths with no override flag; a fixture would have to reproduce all three.

Regenerates the CLI reference from src/cli.ts and diffs it against the committed doc; both paths are fixed with no root flag, so the fixture needs a parseable cli.ts and the generated doc, not a planted file.
Takes --dir, but compares a fully rendered target tree against the .codex/ template corpus; the bad fixture is a generated project with one divergence, which this pass did not build.
Takes --repo, but reconciles .claude/ against .codex/ across commands, agents and skills at once; a bad fixture must reproduce both trees coherently enough that only the planted divergence differs.
Reads the invariant catalog and the emitted global-invariants surface from fixed repo-relative paths under process.cwd(), with no catalog/target override flags to point at a fixture.
Reads .claude/settings.json and .claude/CLAUDE.md from fixed repo-relative paths with no override flag; a fixture cannot be injected without adding one.
Reconciles src/kit/catalog.json against the build-derived src/kit/derived.json from fixed paths under process.cwd(); a fixture must also reproduce the derivation step, not just the two files.
Takes --dir, but reconciles every check-all.mjs step against the CI workflow surface; the bad fixture is a complete local-plus-CI pair with exactly one step missing, which this pass did not build.
Reads package.json plus several documentation surfaces from fixed repo-relative paths with no override flag; there is no injection point for a fixture without changing the gate.

Diffs generated llms.txt content against llms-txt.config.json plus the live docs/INDEX.md doc count; a fixture needs a full parseable config and index pair, not a single planted file, and --check's drift arm was out of scope for this pass.

Diffs live TypeScript export declarations (via a comment-strip/normalize pass over real source files) against committed api/*.api.md snapshots, with ROOT fixed to process.cwd() and no override flag; a fixture needs real parseable TS sources plus a matching snapshot, not a planted file.

Has --standards, but validates YAML registries against threshold_ref cross-references and a risk taxonomy; a bad fixture needs a coherent registry-plus-thresholds pair with exactly one planted violation, which this pass did not build.

Has --dir, but its violation surface (continue-on-error step scoping, merge-gate base-branch filters, informational-workflow allowlists) is intricate multi-rule YAML parsing; a fixture confident enough to discriminate cleanly on one specific rule was not built this pass.

Has --dir, but longest-chain DAG analysis over needs: edges with per-filename-prefix overrides (01-pr-fast/05-release/nightly etc.) needs a carefully constructed multi-job workflow fixture to avoid a brittle proof; not attempted this pass.

Scans many hardcoded reference surfaces at once (check-all.mjs, scripts/**, .claude/hooks/**, settings.json, Makefile, githooks, workflows, run.sh, package.json) with no root-injection flag; reproducing a coherent subset for a bad/clean pair is a larger fixture than this pass scoped.

Regenerates examples/ via a real `arbiter init` child-process run against the built dist/cli.js and diffs the result; a fixture needs a full generator run per --check invocation, not a planted file, and dist/cli.js is not guaranteed built in every test environment.
